supersedes: submissions/bls12-381-g1-ecdlp/partial-cheon-v4 (rejected: sort/lookup ledgers omitted record moves, addressing and index arithmetic; buffered merge sort needs linear auxiliary storage; equal-x keys identify points only up to negation)
work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = m*(64+0.256+3.8025) + m*(64+0.256+1.475) + <= 2^21.9 with m = isqrt(floor(2N/5)) + 1, N = (r-1)/2^20; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. Score = log2(W(2^20)).
heuristics: None for the success probability: k1 is uniform over [0,N) (the d-th power map is exactly d-to-1 onto the order-N subgroup); block j covers exactly the m values {(m1*j + i) mod N : i < m} with consecutive arcs disjoint (start spacing m1 > m, no start collisions for window spans), so every offset covers at least (m-1)m values - an exact per-offset bound of 0.4 - 2^-118 >= 0.39 including all wrap-around hits; the closed form is additionally crosschecked against an exhaustive every-offset brute force on five smaller parameter sets.

The table machinery is deterministic and worst-case exact with every instruction charged: merge sort over an auxiliary buffer (117 passes x (50 move + 15 compare) instructions per baby), binary search (exactly 118 probes x 25 instructions per lookup), comb multiplications (32-40 window additions by count, charged 64 units), mod-r multiplication (explicit 5x52 schoolbook + Montgomery construction, 512 instructions). The sort key is (x, y mod 2), which uniquely determines an affine point on this odd-prime curve (same-x points have opposite y-parities), so every key match is an exact point match and k1 = (i + m1*j) mod N is exact with no sign ambiguity.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold; deterministic full coverage costs about +0.86 log2.
The bound applies only for n >= 2^20; smaller n would force a smaller divisor of r-1.
Peak memory is the main sorted array plus the merge buffer, strictly above 2^124.77 bytes, reported rounded up as 124.8.
Cheon's auxiliary-input attack is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel algorithm; first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
